assumptions: ET0 by FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (Eq. 6) from NASA POWER daily Tmax, Tmin, dew point, 2 m wind and all-sky shortwave radiation, site elevation 19 m (POWER cell); G = 0. Days missing any input are missing, never filled.

Kc mid and Kc end adjusted for climate by FAO-56 Eq. 62 and Eq. 65 with each planting's stage-mean POWER wind (u2) and RHmin (from dew point and Tmax), kept within FAO-56 limits (u2 1–6 m/s, RHmin 20–80 %), and the Table 12 crop height (midpoint of a printed range); Kc end below 0.45 is not adjusted; crops without a printed height (winter wheat on non-frozen soil) keep the table values.

Runoff by the NRCS curve-number method (NEH 630 Table 9-1, good condition, straight rows; bare fallow between crops) for hydrologic soil group C, average antecedent moisture; no capillary rise; water above field capacity drains the same day.

Soil water carries over from crop to crop through fallow periods (continuous daily balance). Bare-soil evaporation by FAO-56 Ch. 7 with Kc,max 1.20 and TEW/REW from Table 19 for the coarse (loamy sand range) implied by the soil's water capacity. Each chain of cycles starts at field capacity (a dry-start case is shown as sensitivity); with three or more cycles in a chain the first is spin-up only.
Roots grow from 0.15 m at planting to the FAO-56 Table 22 upper depth by the end of development.

Flooded (paddy) rice: irrigation need by FAO Irrigation Water Management Training Manual No. 3 §4.4 — ETc (FAO-56 rice Kc) + 200 mm land soaking in the 30 days before planting + percolation and seepage 6 mm/day (the manual's average; heavy clay 4, sandy soil 8) + 100 mm water layer at transplanting − effective rain (0.8P − 25 above 75 mm/month, else 0.6P − 10), per calendar month. No water stress under ponding; the next crop starts at field capacity after draining. Nursery water is not included.
Stage proportions from the FAO-56 Table 11 example closest in total length, scaled to the local season length.
Whole field; frost and hot days use coarse-cell air temperature (exposure, not crop damage).
Priorities not recorded: all six weighted equally (3).
reviewQuestions: Do you have the equipment and labour to plant and harvest each crop shown?
Is there a market for each alternative crop near you?

efficiency.method: Basin (flooded plots): lower end of the attainable range (FAO W4367E, Keller 1992)

comparison.energyRankingNote: Ordered by yearly pumping energy in the high scenario over the replay window (the same weather years and assumptions for every option; one window can be wetter or drier than the median year shown on each card). This is one trade-off, not a new rotation ranking; hard agronomic constraints and your priorities still decide the comparison.

assumptions: Water density 1000 kg/m³ and gravity 9.81 m/s².

Application efficiency 70 % (stated assumption, Basin (flooded plots): lower end of the attainable range (FAO W4367E, Keller 1992)) and conveyance efficiency 100 % (stated assumption), each applied once to net need.
Pump-and-motor efficiency 45 % at the motor terminals; controller/inverter efficiency 95 % between the PV array and the motor; array performance ratio 0.75 (excluding the controller).
Pumping 8 h on each irrigation day; flow = daily volume ÷ pumping time, averaged within each month.
Pipe friction by Darcy–Weisbach with the Swamee–Jain friction factor; fittings as Σ K · v²/2g; the outlet velocity head is included.
Steady flow within a month; no pump curve, suction-lift or cavitation check (no pump model is selected).

Solar: NASA POWER all-sky horizontal irradiation 2016-01-01 to 2025-12-31, monthly means used as peak sun hours. Panels' tilt and local shading are not modelled. Historical averages are not a forecast.
gaps: Pipe length is a hypothetical range, not a surveyed route.
Groundwater depth is a hypothetical range chosen for sensitivity, not a measurement.
Source capacity and water allowance are unknown, so water-supply feasibility is unknown. Mapping a water body does not show how much water may be taken, its dry-season level, ownership or permission.

solarFrom.cellNote: All-sky irradiation on a horizontal surface for the POWER solar grid cell (≈ 1° × 1°), not measured at the field. Local shading is unknown.

water.note: Well depth, drawdown and pipe length are hypothetical example ranges, not measurements.
